title: CoWriter: Guiding Methodological and Synergetic Human-LLM Co-Authoring
title_zh: CoWriter：引导方法论性与协同性的人-LLM 共同写作

paragraphs.en: While LLMs have transformed text generation, standard chat-and-canvas interfaces often reduce human authoring to quite passive supervision, causing review fatigue, over-reliance on AI, and the sidelining of the human role in long-form, source-grounded writing. Prior systems typically address isolated writing phases, leaving comprehensive end-to-end human-LLM collaboration largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce CoWriter , a proactive agentic scheme that adapts expert human (co-)authoring methodologies from cognitive science to flexibly steer the entire writing workflow while actively encouraging the user to engage. In an exploratory user study, compared to a standard LLM baseline, authors using CoWriter better expressed their perspectives and maintained a higher sense of document ownership, supported quantitatively by 2.2 × 2.2\times more successful agent engagements. Furthermore, external reader judges rated the resulting texts higher in ‘‘human touch’’ qualities like storytelling and integrating unique personal experiences. Overall, our results demonstrate that proactively engaging users through established human practices is beneficial for effective LLM-supported co-authoring, providing useful methodologies, techniques and insights for future research on collaborative agents. 1 1 1 Code and dataset will be released upon publication.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管大语言模型已经改变了文本生成方式，但标准的对话加画布式界面往往将人类写作简化为相当被动的监督，导致审阅疲劳、对 AI 的过度依赖，以及在长篇、基于来源的写作中人类角色的边缘化。 以往的系统通常只针对孤立的写作阶段，对全面的人类与大语言模型端到端协作的探索仍基本空白。 在本文中，我们提出了 CoWriter，一种主动式智能体方案，它将认知科学中的专家级人类（协同）写作方法加以适配，灵活地引导整个写作流程，同时积极鼓励用户参与。 在一项探索性用户研究中，与标准大语言模型基线相比，使用 CoWriter 的作者能够更好地表达自己的观点，并保持更高的文档掌控感，这一结果在定量上得到了 2.2 × 2.2\times 更高的智能体成功介入率的支持。 此外，外部读者评审认为最终生成的文本在叙事性和融入独特个人经历等“人性化”特质上得分更高。 总体而言，我们的结果表明，通过既有的人类实践主动吸引用户参与，有利于实现有效的大语言模型支持下的协同写作，并为未来协作智能体的研究提供了有益的方法、技术与洞见。 1 1 1 代码和数据集将在论文发表后发布。

paragraphs.en: Writing has been a fundamental human activity for millennia. Recently, though, Large Language Models (LLMs) have reshaped how we create texts, making LLM-assisted writing one of the most widespread uses of these models ( Chatterji et al., 2025 ) . Nowadays, authors increasingly rely on LLMs, through standard chat or interactive canvas interfaces, to alleviate demanding authoring tasks like synthesizing sources and drafting large blocks of content ( Mysore et al., 2025 ) . LLMs now significantly lower the writing barrier with fast, fluent text generation, empowering a diverse range of users to compose complex, multi-page documents.

Indeed, few recent works explored improving human-LLM co-authoring processes, addressing concrete aspects such as pre-writing brainstorming Jiang et al. (2024) , outlining Zhang et al. (2026) and turn-based initiative-taking Shao et al. (2026) . However, an agentic scheme that actively engages the human throughout the entire co-authoring process, from brainstorming to reviewing, remains under-explored.

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we propose a novel approach towards bridging these gaps in the complex setting of long-form, source-grounded authoring. Our research hypothesis is that effective synergetic human-LLM co-authoring may be achieved by properly adapting established expert methodologies for human-human co-authoring. To explore it, we present CoWriter , an agentic scheme following the seminal cognitive-science work of Flower and Hayes (1981) and its prominent extension to writing teams by Lowry et al. (2004) . These works formalize distinct writing activities (such as brainstorming, outlining, drafting, and reviewing) and, for teams, collaborator roles (e.g., leaders, writers, and reviewers). Our adaptation steers the writing process flexibly through these activities, while keeping the human author fully engaged and influential all along.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们提出了一种新方法，旨在在长篇、基于源文本的写作这一复杂场景中弥合这些差距。 我们的研究假设是，通过恰当地借鉴成熟的人类-人类协作写作专家方法论，可以实现有效的人与大语言模型（LLM）协同写作。 为探索这一假设，我们提出了 CoWriter，一种智能体化方案，它遵循 Flower 和 Hayes（1981）的开创性认知科学工作，以及 Lowry 等人（2004）对其在写作团队方面的著名扩展。 这些工作形式化了不同的写作活动（如头脑风暴、列提纲、起草和审阅），并针对团队形式化了协作者角色（如领导者、写作者和审阅者）。 我们的适配方案通过这些活动灵活地引导写作过程，同时使人类作者始终保持充分的参与和影响力。

paragraphs.en: The key component of our co-authoring framework (§ 3 ) is an agentic lead co-author that guides the writing process through the methodology’s activities, while letting both authors move between them flexibly. Throughout the process, the agent keeps the human co-author engaged and in control of shaping perspectives, steering the narrative, and verifying claims. Following these methodologies, our scheme includes a monitoring component that oversees the writing progress and keeps the lead agent aligned with the methodical workflow, and a “fresh” reviewer agent that provides objective external feedback, unbiased by the writing history.
paragraphs.zh: 我们协同写作框架（§ 3）的核心组件是一个充当主导合著者的智能体，它通过该方法论的各项活动引导写作过程，同时允许两位作者在这些活动之间灵活切换。 在整个过程中，智能体始终让人类合著者保持参与，并由其掌控观点的塑造、叙事的走向以及论断的核实。 遵循这些方法论，我们的方案包含一个监督写作进度并确保主导智能体符合规范化工作流程的监控组件，以及一个提供客观外部反馈、不受写作历史偏见的“全新”审稿智能体。

paragraphs.en: To assess the utility of CoWriter for human users, we devise a comprehensive evaluation scheme that involves author-centric assessments alongside objective measurements of the co-authoring session trajectories (e.g., writing-activity coverage and user engagement) and the eventual written document. In our experiments, 14 participants each co-authored a document once with our agentic system and once with a typical baseline setting involving a frontier LLM chat, canvas and source documents. Notably, with CoWriter , authors felt substantially more comfortable and engaged throughout the authoring process and more successful in expressing their own perspectives, leading to a much higher sense of ownership of the final document. Further, CoWriter elicited about twice as many successful agent engagements as the baseline LLM setting. From an external reader’s assessment, documents produced with CoWriter were found to be more appealing in “human touch” quality aspects, such as expressing unique ideas and the author’s personal experience, storytelling and being more naturally read.
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估 CoWriter 对人类用户的效用，我们设计了一套全面的评估方案，既包括以作者为中心的评估，也包括对共同写作会话轨迹（如写作活动覆盖率和用户参与度）以及最终成文的客观测量。 在我们的实验中，14 名参与者分别用我们的智能体系统和用典型的基线设置（涉及前沿大语言模型聊天、画布和源文档）各共同写作一份文档。 值得注意的是，使用 CoWriter 时，作者在整个写作过程中感觉更加自在、投入度更高，并且更成功地表达了自己的观点，从而对最终文档产生了更强的归属感。 此外，CoWriter 引发的成功智能体参与次数约为基线大语言模型设置的两倍。 从外部读者的评估来看，用 CoWriter 生成的文档在“人情味”质量方面更具吸引力，例如表达独特的想法和作者的个人经历、讲故事以及读起来更自然。

paragraphs.en: In summary, our contributions include: (1) proposing an agentic harness scheme that effectively incorporates established human co-authoring methodologies to lead and engage the user throughout the entire writing process (§ 3 ); (2) introducing an evaluation scheme for human-LLM co-authoring, with a user study design, protocol, and measures incorporating both author-centric and objective assessments of process engagement and output traits (§ 4 ); (3) conducting an elaborate user study, which assesses the utility of our proposed framework and provides valuable results and insights for future research (§ 5 ). Overall, our findings indicate that human co-writing methods transfer well to human-LLM schemes, while human involvement remains valuable, and that our method provides useful techniques and insights for future work on human-LLM co-authoring.
paragraphs.zh: 综上所述，我们的贡献包括：（1）提出一种智能体框架方案，有效地融入了成熟的人机协作写作方法，在整个写作过程中引导并吸引用户（§ 3）；（2）引入一套人-大语言模型协作写作的评估方案，包括用户研究的设计、流程与测量指标，同时涵盖以作者为中心的评估以及对过程参与度和产出特性的客观评估（§ 4）；（3）开展了一项精细的用户研究，评估了我们所提框架的效用，并为未来研究提供了有价值的结果与洞见（§ 5）。 总体而言，我们的研究结果表明，人类协作写作方法可以很好地迁移到人-大语言模型协作方案中，同时人类参与仍然具有价值；我们的方法为未来人-大语言模型协作写作研究提供了有用的技术与洞见。

paragraphs.en: Assisting humans to write and express knowledge has long been a research goal, predating LLMs by decades ( Engelbart, 1962 ) . Unlike fully automatic text generation, human–LLM co-authoring combines the strengths of LLMs with human contributions, perspectives, and editorial control.

paragraphs.en: We focus on proactive agentic behavior that orchestrates an established authoring methodology while sustaining user engagement, thereby mitigating the “human-sidelining” effect that writers report ( Zhao et al., 2025 ; Reza et al., 2025 ) . paragraphs.en: Research in cognitive science and collaborative writing has extensively studied how skilled authors operate, providing a strong empirical foundation for our method design. Single-author writing is widely modeled as an iterative process of planning, translating, and reviewing, coordinated by a central monitor ( Flower and Hayes, 1981 ) , rather than a linear progression toward a final document. During this process, an expert writer engages in knowledge-transforming , i.e., reshaping content according to goals and audience, rather than simply knowledge-telling ( Bereiter and Scardamalia, 1987 ) . Specific stages within this process are associated with better documents, including rich initial goal setting to define the task ( Flower and Hayes, 1980 ) , dedicated pre-writing brainstorming ( Graham and Perin, 2007 ) , and formal outlining prior to drafting ( Kellogg, 1988 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 认知科学与协作写作领域已经广泛研究了熟练作者是如何进行写作的，为我们的方法设计提供了坚实的实证基础。 单作者写作被广泛建模为一个由中央监控器（ Flower and Hayes, 1981 ）协调的计划、转译与审阅的迭代过程，而非朝最终文档线性推进的过程。 在这一过程中，专家作者进行的是知识转化，即根据目标和读者重塑内容，而非单纯的知识陈述（ Bereiter and Scardamalia, 1987 ）。 该过程中的特定阶段与更好的文档相关联，包括用于界定任务的丰富的初始目标设定（ Flower and Hayes, 1980 ）、专门的写前头脑风暴（ Graham and Perin, 2007 ），以及起草前的正式列提纲（ Kellogg, 1988 ）。

paragraphs.en: In multi-author settings, poorly organized collaboration often becomes inefficient and frustrating ( Ede and Lunsford, 1990 ) . Notably, this taxonomy formalizes distinct activities (brainstorming, outlining, drafting, reviewing, revising, and copyediting) alongside specific roles, such as leaders, writers, and reviewers ( Posner and Baecker, 1992 ) .

paragraphs.en: This section introduces CoWriter , an agent-based platform for the co-authoring task (§ 3.1 ) designed to lead a methodological co-writing process (§ 3.2 ; Figure 1 ). The system includes a main agent to direct the workflow and engage the human co-author (§ 3.3 ; Table 1 ), a monitor to oversee the writing process (§ 3.3.2 ), and a reviewer agent to provide external “objective” feedback (§ 3.4 ). We then deploy CoWriter (§ 4 ) to assess the benefits of this guided approach (§ 5 ).
paragraphs.zh: 本节介绍 CoWriter，这是一个基于智能体的共同写作任务平台（§ 3.1），旨在引导一个方法性的共写过程（§ 3.2；图 1）。 该系统包含一个主导工作流并与人类共同作者互动的主智能体（§ 3.3；表 1）、一个监督写作过程的监视器（§ 3.3.2），以及一个提供外部“客观”反馈的审阅智能体（§ 3.4）。 随后我们部署 CoWriter（§ 4）以评估这种引导式方法的收益（§ 5）。

paragraphs.en: We extend the collaborative human-agent authoring task from prior work ( Jiang et al., 2024 ; Shao et al., 2026 ) to a source-grounded setting, where we focus on authoring long documents with explicit structure (i.e., hierarchically titled sections) whose content relies substantially on given (and cited) source documents. To maintain faithfulness to the sources and enable effective content verification ( Gao et al., 2023 ) , we expect that any information requiring citation (e.g., not insights and perspectives of the author, or functional statements; Zhang et al., 2025 ) would explicitly reference supporting evidence in the source documents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将先前工作（Jiang et al., 2024；Shao et al., 2026）中的「人-智能体协作写作」任务扩展到一种基于源文档的设定，在该设定中，我们关注撰写具有显式结构（即带有层级标题的章节）的长文档，其内容在很大程度上依赖于给定的（并被引用的）源文档。 为了保持对源文档的忠实性并实现有效的内容核查（Gao et al., 2023），我们期望任何需要引用的信息（例如，不包括作者本人的洞见与观点，或功能性陈述；Zhang et al., 2025）都应明确指向源文档中的支撑证据。

paragraphs.en: The CoWriter environment employs an augmented chat-and-canvas layout (left part of Figure 1 ). Similar to standard chat-assisted writing, it includes a chat-based message queue for human-agent communication, and a canvas for joint document authoring. In addition, following Shao et al. paragraphs.en: To translate expert human-human co-authoring dynamics into an agentic architecture ( Yao et al., 2023 ; Guo et al., 2024 ) , we distill collaborative concepts from established writing models ( Flower and Hayes, 1981 ; Lowry et al., 2004 , § 2.2 ;) , mapping the core co-authoring roles directly onto three agentic components: the Leader , Monitor and Reviewer ( Figure 1 , right). Implemented via system prompts and tool use, these components dynamically accommodate the non-linear iterative nature of human writing rather than enforcing a rigid sequential workflow, as our transition analysis confirms (§ 5.1 ).
paragraphs.zh: 为了将专家级的人类共同写作动态转化为一种智能体架构（Yao et al., 2023；Guo et al., 2024），我们从已有的写作模型（Flower and Hayes, 1981；Lowry et al., 2004，§2.2）中提炼协作概念，将核心的共同写作角色直接映射到三个智能体组件上：领导者（Leader）、监控者（Monitor）和评审者（Reviewer）（图1，右）。 这些组件通过系统提示词和工具使用来实现，能够动态适应人类写作的非线性迭代特性，而不是强加僵化的顺序化流程，正如我们的转移分析所证实的（§5.1）。

paragraphs.en: The Leader agent (§ 3.3 ) functions as the process lead Lowry et al. (2004) , fully participating in the writing itself and guiding the workflow while motivating and encouraging the users to be active as well. To support both the Leader and the user, a separate Monitor component (§ 3.3.2 ) acts as a writing strategist to track overarching progress and dictate transitions between authoring stages Flower and Hayes (1981) . The Reviewer agent (§ 3.4 ) functions as an on-demand external reviewer , providing feedback on the document free from the inherent biases that both the Leader and the user develop during the writing process. In this environment, the human collaborator both directly co-authors the text and interacts with the Leader .

paragraphs.en: Primarily, the Leader is instructed to proactively guide the user through the co-authoring activities, rather than simply following user instructions, as the writing-activity coverage results in § 5.1 show. At the same time, it is directed to comply with ad hoc user requests even when they deviate from the workflow ( in Table 1 ). To facilitate a methodological workflow, 2 2 2 The workflow is laid out in one prompt, and not split to components, to allow flexibility to maneuver between steps non-sequentially. each of the seven steps is defined using structured fields: (a) step transitions , which define when to trigger the step, the typical number of turns, and possible transitions to other steps; (b) the goal of the step alongside a series of actions to fulfill it; (c) environment actions specifying how to interact with the sources, canvas, and chat (e.g., exploring sources or updating the document outline); and (d) invites , which are proactive suggestions to encourage step-relevant user engagement (see below). Finally, when the user edits the document, the Leader proactively acts upon the revisions rather than waiting for explicit instructions. For example, renaming an entity in the text will trigger the Leader (via the Monitor ; § 3.3.2 ) to proactively update the remaining entity mentions throughout the document.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，正如 § 5.1 的写作活动覆盖结果所示，Leader 被指示主动引导用户完成共同写作活动，而不是仅仅遵循用户的指令。 同时，它也被要求满足用户临时提出的请求，即使这些请求偏离了（表 1 中的）工作流程。 为了促进方法论式的工作流程，2 2 2 工作流程被置于一个提示中，而非拆分到各个组件，以便灵活地在各步骤之间非顺序地切换。七个步骤中的每一步都通过结构化字段来定义：(a) 步骤转换（step transitions），定义何时触发该步骤、典型的对话轮数以及可能转换到的其他步骤；(b) 该步骤的目标以及实现目标的一系列动作；(c) 环境动作（environment actions），规定如何与来源、画布和聊天进行交互（例如探索来源或更新文档大纲）；以及 (d) 邀请（invites），即鼓励用户参与与步骤相关互动的主动建议（见下文）。 最后，当用户编辑文档时，Leader 会主动根据这些修改采取行动，而不是等待明确的指令。 例如，在文本中重命名某个实体会触发 Leader（通过 Monitor；§ 3.3.2）主动更新文档中其余该实体的所有提及处。

paragraphs.en: To promote user engagement and prevent the human from being sidelined in the co-authoring process, the per-step invite instructions specify targeted step-relevant actions to encourage participation (right column of Table 1 ). The agent adapts its invitations to the current step by asking questions, proposing alternatives, requesting feedback, or soliciting the user’s own ideas. Complementarily, when handling ad hoc user requests, the prompt instructs the agent to finish each turn with a follow-up option related to the request, alongside an option to return (or proceed) to the most appropriate workflow step. For example, if a user asks about information in the sources, the agent might offer to incorporate the resulting insight into the document or alternatively to move on to the next step. To further restrain the LLM from sidelining the user, the agent is directed to maintain a conversational cadence through short bite-sized interactions and incremental document updates, manageable for the human co-author. To assist the user in tracing source information, the agent anchors claims via citations to specific source spans rather than to full documents ( Slobodkin et al., 2024 ; Hirsch et al., 2025 ) . Finally, the user is kept engaged via an updated Writing Log widget, maintained by the Monitor , that displays the current process state (example in Figure 21 , App. C ).
paragraphs.zh: 为了提升用户参与度并防止人类在共同创作过程中被边缘化，每一步的邀请指令会指定与当前步骤相关的针对性行动以鼓励参与（表1右栏）。 智能体通过提问、提出备选方案、请求反馈或征询用户自己的想法，使其邀请适应当前步骤。 与之互补的是，在处理用户临时请求时，提示词指示智能体在每轮对话结束时给出一个与该请求相关的后续选项，同时提供一个返回（或前往）最合适工作流步骤的选项。 例如，如果用户询问来源中的信息，智能体可能会提议将由此得到的洞见写入文档，或者建议转入下一步。 为了进一步约束大语言模型、避免其边缘化用户，智能体被要求通过简短的交互式对话和渐进式文档更新来保持对话节奏，使人类共同创作者能够轻松应对。 为了帮助用户追溯来源信息，智能体通过引用具体来源片段而非整篇文档来锚定论断（Slobodkin et al., 2024；Hirsch et al., 2025）。 最后，通过一个由 Monitor 维护、实时更新的写作日志小部件来展示当前流程状态，使用户保持参与（示例见图21，附录C）。

paragraphs.en: During complex authoring processes, both human writers and LLM-based agents can drift off-track, necessitating a governing element. To maintain focus, human cognitive models describe a central monitor ( Flower and Hayes, 1981 ) , and recent agentic systems employ mechanisms to moderate the process ( Jiang et al., 2024 ; Balepur et al., 2025 ) . Inspired by these concepts, the Monitor is an LLM-based component embedded within the Leader . It observes environment events — such as document updates and user messages — and tracks progress along the workflow steps.
paragraphs.zh: 在复杂的写作过程中，人类作者和基于 LLM 的智能体都可能偏离轨道，因此需要一个统筹性的要素。 为了保持专注，人类认知模型描述了一个中央监控器（Flower and Hayes, 1981），而近期的智能体系统也采用了调节过程的机制（Jiang et al., 2024；Balepur et al., 2025）。 受这些概念启发，Monitor（监控器）是一个嵌入在 Leader（领导者）之中的基于 LLM 的组件。 它观察环境事件——例如文档更新和用户消息——并跟踪工作流各步骤的进展。

Further details are in App. D .

paragraphs.en: Delegating critique to a separate agent follows prior multi-agent writing systems that decouple generation from review to reduce confirmation bias and identify a broader range of issues ( Bae and Kim, 2024 ; Hong et al., 2024 ) . In the collaborative-writing taxonomy of Lowry et al. (2004) , a reviewer evaluates the document without participating in its writing. Accordingly, Reviewer simulates an external reviewer from the target audience.

paragraphs.en: Our experiments evaluate whether guiding users through a methodical workflow leads to an effective collaborative writing process and produces a source-grounded document that users can confidently approve. We describe our user study comparing CoWriter against a baseline (§ 4.1 ), followed by our evaluation dimensions for both the co-authoring sessions and the final outputs (§ 4.2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们的实验评估：通过一个有条理的工作流引导用户，是否能带来高效的协作写作过程，并产出一篇有来源依据、用户可以有信心批准的文档。 我们描述了将 CoWriter 与基线进行比较的用户研究（§ 4.1），随后介绍针对共同写作会话和最终产出的评估维度（§ 4.2）。

sents.en: Our experiments evaluate whether guiding users through a methodical workflow leads to an effective collaborative writing process and produces a source-grounded document that users can confidently approve.
sents.zh: 我们的实验评估：通过一个有条理的工作流引导用户，是否能带来高效的协作写作过程，并产出一篇有来源依据、用户可以有信心批准的文档。

sents.en: We describe our user study comparing CoWriter against a baseline (§ 4.1 ), followed by our evaluation dimensions for both the co-authoring sessions and the final outputs (§ 4.2 ).
sents.zh: 我们描述了将 CoWriter 与基线进行比较的用户研究（§ 4.1），随后介绍针对共同写作会话和最终产出的评估维度（§ 4.2）。

paragraphs.en: The study simulates a realistic long-form writing task requiring prolonged human-agent interaction. Participants collaboratively authored a 750–1000 word blog post on a specified topic, grounded in provided sources. To elicit meaningful, active user contributions, we instructed participants to act as a popular blogger , tasking them with combining factual claims from the sources with their own perspectives , personal experiences , and illustrative examples (full details in App. F ).
paragraphs.zh: 该研究模拟了一项需要长时间人机交互的现实长文写作任务。 参与者围绕指定主题，基于所提供的资料，协作撰写一篇750至1000字的博客文章。 为了引出有意义的、主动的用户贡献，我们要求参与者扮演一位知名博主，让他们将来自资料的事实性观点与自己的看法、个人经历以及说明性例子结合起来（完整细节见附录F）。

paragraphs.en: We adapted four everyday-life blog topics from the DREsS dataset ( Yoo et al., 2025 ) (e.g., “The Impact of Smartphones on Family and Friend Communication” ), manually chosen to satisfy three criteria: (i) they are easy to understand and sufficiently engaging for non-expert writers, (ii) all topics encourage participants to contribute personal perspectives and experiences, and (iii) they are comparable in complexity and writing difficulty. For each topic, we manually curated ten relevant diverse academic research papers. To keep the reading load manageable, each source was required to be academically credible, relevant, permissively licensed, and under 20 pages (see App. G ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们从 DREsS 数据集（Yoo et al., 2025）中选取了四个日常生活中的博客主题（例如“智能手机对家人与朋友沟通的影响”），并经过人工挑选以满足三个标准：（i）主题易于理解且对非专业写作者有足够的吸引力；（ii）所有主题都能鼓励参与者贡献个人观点和经验；（iii）各主题在复杂度和写作难度上具有可比性。 针对每个主题，我们人工筛选了十篇相关的、多样化的学术研究论文。 为了将阅读负担控制在可承受范围内，每个文献来源都必须具备学术可信性、相关性、宽松的许可协议，并且篇幅不超过 20 页（见附录 G）。

paragraphs.en: We compared CoWriter against a control baseline that simulates a standard LLM-assisted setup of a chat, a document canvas, and uploaded sources, excluding the components supporting our co-authoring workflow and user engagement. To ensure a fair comparison, both systems share the exact same environment and underlying model. 3 3 3 All systems and agents run on a claude-sonnet-4.6 backbone model with low thinking effort, to balance performance and response time. To mitigate possible confounding variables, we stripped our collaborative mechanisms: we modified the Leader prompt to remove the workflow and engagement instructions, and disabled the other two agentic components, the Writing Log , and localized attribution.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将 CoWriter 与一个对照基线进行了比较，该基线模拟了标准的 LLM 辅助设置，即聊天、文档画布和上传来源，但不包含支持我们共同写作工作流和用户参与度的组件。 为确保公平比较，两个系统使用完全相同的环境和底层模型。所有系统和智能体均运行在 claude-sonnet-4.6 主干模型上，并采用较低的思考强度，以平衡性能与响应时间。 为减少可能的混淆变量，我们移除了我们的协作机制：我们修改了 Leader 的提示词以删除工作流和参与度指令，并禁用了另外两个智能体组件，即写作日志（Writing Log）和局部归因（localized attribution）。

paragraphs.en: Fourteen graduate students with academic writing experience participated in a within-subjects study. 4 4 4 We conducted a 3-participant pilot prior to the full study to refine the system and experimental protocol. Following an orientation and 15 minutes of guided practice per system, participants completed two writing sessions on different topics — one with CoWriter and one with the baseline. To encourage realistic iterative writing and source exploration, each session was intended to last up to 75 minutes, with the second session occurring within 48 hours of the first. We counterbalanced both the system order and the topic-to-system assignment, ensuring that all topics appeared approximately equally often in both conditions. Participants completed post-session questionnaires after each task, followed by a final comparative survey upon finishing both. Recruitment and procedural details are in App. H .
paragraphs.zh: 十四名具有学术写作经验的研究生参与了一项被试内研究。4 4 4 在正式研究之前，我们进行了一个三人参与者的试点研究，以完善系统和实验方案。 在完成介绍环节以及每个系统 15 分钟的引导练习后，参与者完成了两次不同主题的写作任务——一次使用 CoWriter，一次使用基线系统。 为了鼓励真实的迭代写作和来源探索，每次写作环节的时长设计为最多 75 分钟，第二次写作环节在第一次写作环节的 48 小时内进行。 我们对系统顺序以及主题与系统的分配进行了平衡，确保所有主题在两种条件下出现的频率大致相等。 参与者在每次任务结束后填写写作环节后问卷，并在完成两次任务后填写最终的对比调查。 招募与流程细节见附录 H。

paragraphs.en: A comprehensive evaluation of co-authoring requires assessing the system’s impact on both the writing process and the user, rather than just the final text. Accordingly, we evaluate sessions across two dimensions: (1) the authoring process , focusing on workflow adherence, user engagement, and process efficiency; and (2) the produced document , focusing on output quality and human author expression. For both dimensions, we utilize authors’ questionnaire ratings alongside quantitative measurements and external judgments. This section outlines these aspects; full results are in § 5 .
paragraphs.zh: 对协同写作的全面评估，需要考量系统对写作过程和用户两方面的影响，而不仅仅是最终文本。 因此，我们从两个维度评估会话：（1）创作过程，重点关注工作流遵循度、用户参与度和过程效率；（2）生成的文档，重点关注输出质量和人类作者的表达。 对于这两个维度，我们结合作者的问卷评分、定量测量和外部评判。 本节概述这些方面；完整结果见 § 5。

paragraphs.en: To capture user preference and perception, our evaluation relies on a comparative questionnaire. After completing both sessions, participants answered 13 questions on a 5-point scale (ranging from “Prefer System A” to “Prefer System B”), eliciting pairwise preferences on user engagement, the authoring process, output quality, and confidence in the final document. To corroborate these comparative results, participants also completed per-session questionnaires after each task. These measured similar aspects while incorporating standard instruments for cognitive load (adapted from NASA-TLX; Hart and Staveland, 1988 ) and usability ( Finstad, 2010 ) . We observed consistent trends across both questionnaire formats (questions and details in App. I ).
paragraphs.zh: 为了捕捉用户偏好与感知，我们的评估采用了一份对比式问卷。 在完成两个会话后，参与者回答了13个问题，采用5分制（从“偏好系统A”到“偏好系统B”），以获取他们在用户参与度、创作过程、输出质量以及对最终文档的信心方面的成对偏好。 为了佐证这些对比结果，参与者在每项任务结束后还填写了针对单个会话的问卷。 这些问卷测量了类似的方面，同时纳入了认知负荷（改编自NASA-TLX；Hart and Staveland, 1988）和可用性（Finstad, 2010）的标准测量工具。 我们在两种问卷形式中观察到一致的趋势（问题与细节见附录I）。

paragraphs.en: (1) Coverage of writing activities measures a system’s proactive effort to encourage collaboration through the seven writing activities defined in the co-authoring workflow (§ 2.2 ; Table 1 ). It is estimated per activity as the percentage of sessions that include it. To derive these percentages, an LLM 5 5 5 We annotated both writing activities and engagement using claude-opus-4.8 with high reasoning effort. Inter-rater agreement with two human annotators on a 118-message subset yielded an average Cohen’s κ = 0.54 \kappa=0.54 , detailed in App. K . labels each turn in each session with one of the seven activities or ‘other’.

paragraphs.en: (2) Engagement rate measures the number of engagement expressions per 100 words of agent messages, accommodating systems of different verbosity. To quantify this, an LLM 5 marks all phrases within agent turns that express engagement, defined as either a question , a set of options to choose from, an action request , or a next-step proposal .
paragraphs.zh: （2）互动率衡量智能体消息每100词中的互动表达数量，以适配不同冗长程度的系统。 为量化这一点，LLM 5 会对智能体轮次中所有表达互动的短语进行标注，这些短语定义为以下任一形式：提问、供选择的选项集合、行动请求或下一步建议。

paragraphs.en: (3) Successful engagement ratio measures the system’s effectiveness in maintaining user participation. Quantitative engagement metrics in prior work generally focused on the system’s initiations, overlooking the user’s response ( Wu et al., 2025 ; Shao et al., 2026 ) . To capture it, the annotating LLM also marks whether the subsequent user-turns directly respond to each expression. The success ratio is the percentage of engagement expressions that induced a direct user response.
paragraphs.zh: (3) 成功互动率衡量系统在维持用户参与方面的有效性。 以往工作中的定量参与指标通常只关注系统的主动发起，而忽略了用户的回应 (Wu et al., 2025; Shao et al., 2026)。 为了捕捉这一点，标注大语言模型还会标记后续用户轮次是否直接回应了每个参与表达。 成功率是指引发用户直接回应的参与表达所占的百分比。

paragraphs.en: Most notably, human raters preferred CoWriter documents for both Linguistic Fluency and Interestingness , with respective preference rates of 43% and 30% higher than for the baseline. paragraphs.en: We introduced CoWriter , a proactive agentic framework that shifts human-LLM co-authoring from passive text generation to an actively guided, methodical workflow. By adapting expert human writing methodologies, CoWriter leads the entire authoring process while actively eliciting user engagement. Our evaluation demonstrates that this approach significantly improves both the co-authoring process and the final output: CoWriter improved the overall writing experience, increased engagement and ownership, and produced documents preferred by authors, human annotators, and LLM evaluators over a strong control baseline. By demonstrating the value of proactive and methodical guidance, this work provides a foundation for designing user-centered agents and harnesses for a wider range of complex collaborative tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 CoWriter，一个主动式智能体框架，将人与大语言模型的协同写作从被动的文本生成转变为 actively guided、有条理的工作流程。 通过借鉴人类专家的写作方法论，CoWriter 主导整个写作过程，同时主动引导用户参与。 我们的评估表明，这种方法显著改善了协同写作过程和最终成果：与强对照组基线相比，CoWriter 改善了整体写作体验，提高了参与度和主人翁意识，并且其生成的文档更受作者、人工标注者和大语言模型评估者的青睐。 通过展示主动且有条理的引导的价值，这项工作为设计以用户为中心的智能体和工具提供了基础，并可推广至更广泛的复杂协作任务。

paragraphs.en: Although the population size and demography is limited in our user studies (with recruitment conducted through universities for students and graduates), this is common practice in controlled NLP and HCI user studies. Relatedly, the study scope was limited to a moderate number of writing topics (as is common in comparable studies). Conducting large-scale controlled co-authoring studies is inherently expensive and time-intensive, as each session requires long interactive writing periods, extensive source materials, and detailed post-hoc evaluation. Such studies are particularly challenging to scale in academic research settings with limited resources and outreach. Nevertheless, the study was designed with counterbalancing across systems and topics, and combined user feedback, human document assessment, and automatic evaluation to provide multiple complementary perspectives on system behavior. Broader deployment studies across more diverse populations, professional writing settings, and writing genres (e.g., expert or creative writing, where authors may prefer less guidance) would help further validate the generality of our findings and the significance of results.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管我们的用户研究在人口规模和人口统计特征上存在局限（招募通过大学面向学生和毕业生进行），但这在受控的 NLP 和人机交互（HCI）用户研究中是常见做法。 与此相关的是，研究的范围局限于数量适中的写作主题（这在同类研究中也很常见）。 开展大规模受控的合著研究本身就成本高昂且耗时，因为每次会话都需要较长的交互式写作时间、大量的源材料以及详细的事后评估。 在资源和影响力有限的学术研究环境中，此类研究尤其难以规模化。 尽管如此，本研究在设计上采用了跨系统和跨主题的平衡安排，并结合了用户反馈、人工文档评估和自动评估，以便从多个互补的视角审视系统行为。 在更多样化的人群、专业写作场景和写作体裁（例如专家写作或创意写作，作者可能更倾向于较少的指导）中开展更广泛的部署研究，将有助于进一步验证我们研究结果的普遍性和结果的重要性。

paragraphs.en: At the start of a co-authoring session, the underlying LLM is given the system prompt, and the agent greets with a predefined message to the user. Upon a new user message or document update (triggered by Monitor ), the LLM receives the current document, the chat history (as a list of messages), the Writing Log , and a list of system reminders pertaining to the current state of the workflow (see example in Figure 6 ). Accordingly, the LLM executes a ReAct loop ( Yao et al., 2023 ) , interleaving reasoning steps, tool calls, and ending by emitting a final chat message to the user.
paragraphs.zh: 在协作写作会话开始时，底层 LLM 会收到系统提示词，智能体以一条预定义消息向用户问候。 当有新的用户消息或文档更新时（由 Monitor 触发），LLM 会收到当前文档、聊天历史（以消息列表形式）、Writing Log，以及一组与当前工作流状态相关的系统提醒（示例见图 6）。 相应地，LLM 执行一个 ReAct 循环（Yao et al., 2023），交替进行推理步骤和工具调用，最后以向用户发出一条最终聊天消息结束。

paragraphs.en: When Leader is still processing a previous message, the event is queued until processing finishes. When more than one event is enqueued, only the last may trigger the agent. Concurrent document updates (by both Leader and the user) are handled with the Yjs protocol that manages concurrent updates to a shared data structure (the document) in a conflict-free approach ( Nicolaescu et al., 2015 ) . We used the implementation from https://yjs.dev/ .

paragraphs.en: Monitor observes a new event from the user (either a chat message or a document revision) and conditionally triggers Leader . For user messages Monitor always triggers Leader . Whether to trigger on a user revision depends on its decision. Next, Monitor sends Leader a message consisting of the event, the current system reminders, the current document XML ( Figure 25 ), and the Writing Log ( Figure 21 ) for the agent to act on. paragraphs.en: If the response fails to parse, or if any old_text in a writing_log_replacements entry does not match the current Writing Log exactly once, Monitor self-corrects by re-issuing the prompt with the error appended (up to three attempts in total).
paragraphs.zh: 如果响应解析失败，或者 writing_log_replacements 条目中的任何 old_text 与当前 Writing Log 不是恰好匹配一次，Monitor 会通过在错误信息后附加并重新发出提示词来进行自我纠正（总共最多尝试三次）。

paragraphs.en: We followed a system-reminders pattern, as incorporated in the popular coding agent Claude Code. 7 7 7 https://claude.com/product/claude-code Specifically, Monitor wraps each user event (chat message or document update) with a list of system-reminders to notify Leader about the current state of the authoring process and on any open items for possible actions.
paragraphs.zh: 我们采用了系统提醒（system-reminders）模式，这一模式已被流行的编程智能体 Claude Code 所采用。7 7 7 https://claude.com/product/claude-code 具体而言，Monitor（监视器）会用一组系统提醒来包装每个用户事件（聊天消息或文档更新），以通知 Leader（领导者）当前创作过程的状态以及任何待处理的、可能需要采取行动的事项。

paragraphs.en: Status — the current writing activity and word count (computed) vs. target ( Monitor -inferred), plus code-computed signals: [TBD] / [outline] / [in-progress] progress markers in the document, broken citations (named <deeplink> in the prompts), and a flag set when the user has edited the document since Leader ’s last read.
paragraphs.zh: 状态 — 当前的写作活动与字数（由代码计算）与目标（由 Monitor 推断）的对比，以及由代码计算的信号：文档中的 [TBD] / [outline] / [in-progress] 进度标记、损坏的引用（在提示词中命名为 <deeplink>），以及自 Leader 上次读取以来用户是否编辑过文档的标志位。

paragraphs.en: Communication — open questions and open requests still awaiting a reply, each tagged with its direction ( from_user / from_agent ).
paragraphs.zh: 通信 — 仍等待回复的开放问题和开放请求，每个均标注其方向（ from_user / from_agent ）。

paragraphs.en: Feedback — one concise, location-specific sentence flagging the most relevant non-obvious divergence from the Writing Goal or the recent chat, surfaced verbatim as the Monitor ’s steering nudge.

paragraphs.en: The Monitor maintains the four system-reminder sections via per-field delta updates rather than regenerating them from scratch each turn ( Figure 7 ): null leaves the previous value unchanged, [] or "" explicitly clears, and any other value replaces.
paragraphs.zh: 监控器（Monitor）通过按字段的增量更新来维护四个系统提醒部分，而不是每轮从头重新生成（图 7）：null 表示保持先前的值不变，[] 或 "" 表示显式清空，其他任何值则表示替换。

paragraphs.en: The four Status signals are code-computed signals recomputed on every Leader turn from the live document XML and source-file list: the current word count (whitespace-separated word count of the text); the progress-marker list using regex; the broken-deeplinks list (dangling citations to invalid sources or lines) validated against the source files; and the unread-user-edit flag (cleared the next time Leader reads the document).
paragraphs.zh: 四个 Status 信号是每次 Leader 回合从实时文档 XML 和源文件列表重新计算的代码计算信号：当前字数（文本中按空白符分隔的单词数）；使用正则表达式提取的进度标记列表；对照源文件验证的失效深链列表（指向无效源或行的悬空引用）；以及未读用户编辑标志（在 Leader 下一次读取文档时清除）。

paragraphs.en: We developed the questionnaire statements to target our co-authoring process. After each writing session, participants completed a per-system questionnaire of 37 statements rated on a 7-point Likert scale ( Table 6 ). After completing both sessions, they completed a comparative questionnaire of 13 questions rated on a 5-point comparative scale ( Table 7 ). The per-session questionnaire records each system’s rating in isolation, whereas the comparative questionnaire elicits a direct preference between the two. Reporting both lets us cross-check absolute and relative judgments. Reverse-coded statements (marked in Table 6 ) were inverted to < 8 − score > <8-\text{score}> before analysis, so that a higher value always indicates a more positive response. Each per-session questionnaire also included one instructional attention-check item, whose handling is described in Appendix J . The per-session questionnaire additionally measured task load with NASA-TLX items ( Hart and Staveland, 1988 ) and usability with the four-item UMUX scale ( Finstad, 2010 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 我们围绕共同写作流程设计了问卷中的各项陈述。 每次写作环节结束后，参与者填写一份包含37条陈述的针对单个系统的问卷，采用7点李克特量表评分（表6）。 完成两个环节后，他们填写一份包含13个问题的对比问卷，采用5点对比量表评分（表7）。 每次环节的问卷单独记录对每个系统的评分，而对比问卷则引出对两个系统的直接偏好。 同时报告两者使我们能够交叉验证绝对判断与相对判断。 反向计分的陈述（在表6中标注）在分析前被转换为 < 8 − score > <8-\text{score}>，使得数值越高始终代表越积极的回应。 每份针对单个系统的问卷还包含一个指导性的注意力检查项，其处理方式见附录J。 针对单个系统的问卷还通过NASA-TLX量表（Hart and Staveland, 1988）测量任务负荷，并通过四项UMUX量表（Finstad, 2010）测量可用性。

paragraphs.en: One participant (P6) failed an instructional manipulation check ( Oppenheimer et al., 2009 ) in both post-session questionnaires, giving the same wrong answer on both, consistent with item-level acquiescence rather than disengagement. Within-session indicators showed strong engagement: structured task prompts, differentiated per-event quality ratings, and personal anecdotes integrated into both documents. In a structured debrief, P6 accurately recalled both conditions and gave a detailed comparison of the two systems. When asked which system to use next and which was more cognitively demanding, P6 chose the proactive system for future use, describing it as “writing with auxiliary wheels”. P6 identified the baseline as the more demanding of the two, reproducing the per-session direction under blind re-rating. On the four-item Cognitive Load construct (1–7; higher = = more load), proactive = 1.00 =\mathbf{1.00} vs. baseline = 6.25 =\mathbf{6.25} ; on the four-item UMUX usability construct, proactive = 7.00 =\mathbf{7.00} vs. baseline = 6.50 =\mathbf{6.50} – both consistent with the debrief. Following Curran (2016) on combining convergent indicators we retained P6 in the primary analysis.

paragraphs.en: This appendix details the conversation annotations underlying the process metrics (§ 4.2 ), including the LLM procedure, human validation, and inter-rater agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 本附录详细介绍了过程指标（§ 4.2）所依据的对话标注，包括大语言模型（LLM）的处理流程、人工验证以及评分者间一致性。

paragraphs.en: We annotated each session message by prompting an LLM ( claude-opus-4.8 with high reasoning effort) once for each metric:
paragraphs.zh: 我们通过提示一个 LLM（claude-opus-4.8，高推理力度）对每条会话消息按每个指标各标注一次：

paragraphs.en: Writing activities: The model labels each message with the single most prominent writing activity from the seven predefined activities ( Table 1 ), or “other” if none apply (prompt in Figure 23 ).
paragraphs.zh: 写作活动：模型为每条消息标注七个预定义活动（表 1）中最突出的单一写作活动，若均不适用则标注为“其他”（提示词见图 23）。

paragraphs.en: Engagement phrases: The model extracts every engagement expression verbatim from each message, classifying its type (question, choice, action request, or next-step proposal) and whether it was followed up (i.e., directly addressed in the collaborator’s next turn; prompt in Figure 24 ).
paragraphs.zh: 互动短语：模型从每条消息中逐字提取所有互动表达，分类其类型（提问、选择、行动请求或下一步建议），以及是否得到了后续回应（即在协作者的下一轮中是否被直接提及；提示词见图 24）。

paragraphs.en: These message-level annotations (activity type, total engagement expressions, and successful follow-ups) are then aggregated per system to calculate the metrics in § 4.2 .
paragraphs.zh: 这些消息级别的标注（活动类型、总互动表达数和成功后续跟进数）随后按每个系统进行汇总，以计算第 4.2 节中的指标。

paragraphs.en: Two human annotators, both PhD students experienced in English academic writing, independently labeled 118 messages across four sessions (two per system) using the guidelines provided to the LLM. Human–LLM Cohen’s κ \kappa per message was reliable across writing activities ( κ = 0.62 \kappa=0.62 , unweighted), engagement expressions ( κ = 0.46 \kappa=0.46 , quadratic-weighted), and successful engagements ( κ = 0.55 \kappa=0.55 , quadratic-weighted), with an overall mean of κ = 0.54 \kappa=0.54 .
paragraphs.zh: 两名人类标注者均为具有英文学术写作经验的博士生，他们使用提供给大语言模型的指南，对四次会话（每个系统两次）中的118条消息进行了独立标注。 人类与大语言模型在逐条消息上的 Cohen's κ \kappa 在写作活动（ κ = 0.62 \kappa=0.62 ，未加权）、参与度表达（ κ = 0.46 \kappa=0.46 ，二次加权）和成功参与（ κ = 0.55 \kappa=0.55 ，二次加权）方面均具有可靠性，总体均值为 κ = 0.54 \kappa=0.54 。

paragraphs.en: We complement the human reader assessment (§ 5.3 ) with an automatic comparative assessment of all 48 document pairs (12 pairs per topic), each pairing one CoWriter document and one baseline document written on the same topic. Three LLM-as-a-judge models scored every pair on the same 19 comparative questions and grouped into the four aspects. The LLM-as-a-judge models used the same 5-point comparative scale given to the human annotators. Each model was queried once per (pair, aspect) .
paragraphs.zh: 我们在人工读者评估（§ 5.3）的基础上，对所有 48 个文档对（每个主题 12 对）进行了自动化的对比评估，每个文档对由一篇 CoWriter 文档和一篇同一主题的基线文档组成。 三个 LLM-as-a-judge（大模型作为裁判）模型对每个文档对在相同的 19 个对比性问题上打分，并归入四个方面。 这些 LLM-as-a-judge 模型使用了与人工标注者相同的 5 分对比评分量表。 每个模型对每个（文档对，方面）组合只被查询一次。

paragraphs.en: We compared per-construct composite scores between baseline and CoWriter using paired tests over the N = 14 N{=}14 within-subject pairs. The “normality” of the paired differences was assessed via sample skewness and excess kurtosis, following West et al. (1995) , who treat violations as substantial only when | skewness | > 2 |\text{skewness}|\,{>}\,2 or | excess kurtosis | > 7 |\text{excess kurtosis}|\,{>}\,7 . Under these thresholds all constructs except “Document Publish” (skewness = 2.28 =2.28 , excess kurtosis = 5.85 =5.85 ) fell within the mild range and were analyzed with a paired t t -test. For Document Publish we instead report the Wilcoxon signed-rank test ( Wilcoxon, 1945 ) , which does not assume normality of the paired differences. Similarly, we applied this test to the workflow-adherence measures (§ 5.1 and Figure 2 ) as the goal-setting indicator exceeded the skewness threshold ( − 2.29 -2.29 ).
